predictions.reasoning: This market concerns the 2028 US Presidential Election, roughly three years away. A single candidate's implied probability of winning that far out carries essentially no information for public asset prices over a 12-hour window. There is no policy catalyst, no near-term event, and Whitmer is one of many possible nominees. Broad US equities are the most liquid proxy for any political-risk repricing, but the linkage here is negligible; any move in this obscure long-dated market would be pure noise relative to the S&P 500.

evidence_used: Market question targets the 2028 presidential election, ~3 years from now
Whitmer is one of many potential candidates, not an incumbent with immediate policy control
No near-term catalyst or resolution event within the 12h window
Long-dated election odds historically have minimal same-day impact on liquid assets
uncertainty_notes: A sharp probability move could reflect a genuine breaking headline (e.g., candidacy declaration) but even that rarely moves broad indices materially
Sector-level effects (healthcare, energy) from a specific candidate are speculative and long-dated
Prediction-market liquidity for a single 2028 candidate is thin, so probability moves may be noise

llm_justification.summary: The market asks whether Gretchen Whitmer wins the 2028 presidential election, an event three years out involving one of many possible candidates. There is no plausible mechanism for a 12-hour public-asset move of tradable magnitude. Even a sharp shift in her implied odds carries essentially no actionable information for liquid instruments now. The best proxy (SPY) would show no attributable move; direction is unclear and confidence is very low. This is a no-signal mapping.
key_assumptions: No imminent policy or election event within the window
Long-dated single-candidate odds do not materially reprice broad equities
Any observed probability move is likely thin-market noise
failure_modes: A major breaking news event (Whitmer entering race, major scandal) could briefly move sector ETFs, which this card would miss
The proxy (SPY) is essentially unexposed to this specific long-dated political question
Attributing any SPY move to this market would be spurious correlation given macro dominance
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
